quests.partialSentence: The doctor examined ____ carefully and said I was fine.
quests.hint: We need an object pronoun, since this word comes after the verb 'examined.'
quests.explanation: Object pronouns like 'me' follow verbs, so 'examined me' is correct rather than the subject pronoun 'I.'

quests.partialSentence: My sister felt sick, so I took ____ to see a doctor.
quests.hint: We need an object pronoun, since it comes after the verb 'took.'
quests.explanation: 'Her' is the object pronoun that follows the verb 'took,' replacing 'my sister.'

quests.partialSentence: The nurse gave ____ some medicine for the pain.
quests.hint: We need a plural object pronoun after the verb 'gave.'
quests.explanation: 'Us' is the object pronoun matching 'we' and follows the verb 'gave.'

quests.partialSentence: The singer thanked ____ for coming to the concert.
quests.hint: We need an object pronoun after the verb 'thanked.'
quests.explanation: 'Us' is the object pronoun form of 'we,' used after the verb 'thanked.'

quests.partialSentence: I really like this band; their new song makes ____ want to dance.
quests.hint: We need an object pronoun after the verb 'makes.'
quests.explanation: 'Me' is the object pronoun that follows the verb 'makes,' not the subject pronoun 'I.'

quests.partialSentence: The movie was so funny that it made ____ laugh the whole time.
quests.hint: We need a plural object pronoun after the verb 'made.'
quests.explanation: 'Them' is the object pronoun matching 'they,' used after the verb 'made.'

quests.partialSentence: I ____ check my email before I leave for work.
quests.hint: Think about an action that happens every single time, with no exceptions.
quests.explanation: 'Always' shows that something happens 100% of the time, fitting a strict daily habit.

quests.partialSentence: She ____ answers messages late at night because she goes to bed early.
quests.hint: Think about an action that does not happen at all.
quests.explanation: 'Never' shows that an action does not happen at any time, fitting someone who avoids late replies.

quests.partialSentence: We ____ call our grandparents on Sunday afternoons.
quests.hint: Think about something that happens most of the time, but maybe not every single time.
quests.explanation: 'Usually' expresses something that happens most of the time, without being absolute like 'always.'

quests.partialSentence: I ____ make my bed as soon as I wake up.
quests.hint: Think about a habit the speaker does without exception.
quests.explanation: 'Always' fits a consistent daily habit done every time.

quests.partialSentence: He ____ skips breakfast, maybe once or twice a year.
quests.hint: Think about something that almost never happens, but isn't completely impossible.
quests.explanation: 'Rarely' shows something happens very infrequently, unlike 'never,' which means not at all.

quests.partialSentence: We ____ go for a walk after dinner; it's part of our routine.
quests.hint: Think about a habit described as part of a fixed routine.
quests.explanation: 'Always' fits a regular, unbroken routine, such as a daily after-dinner walk.

quests.partialSentence: This year's exam was ____ than last year's.
quests.hint: We're comparing two specific exams, so we need the comparative form.
quests.explanation: When comparing two things, short adjectives add -er, so 'hard' becomes 'harder.'

quests.partialSentence: My new classroom is ____ than my old one.
quests.hint: We're comparing two classrooms, so we need the comparative form.
quests.explanation: Short adjectives like 'bright' form the comparative by adding -er: 'brighter.'

quests.partialSentence: History class is ____ than mathematics class, in my opinion.
quests.hint: This adjective has three syllables, so the comparative is formed differently.
quests.explanation: Longer adjectives like 'interesting' use 'more' instead of an -er ending: 'more interesting.'

quests.partialSentence: This job is ____ than my last one because I work from home.
quests.hint: We're comparing two jobs, so we need the comparative form.
quests.explanation: Adjectives ending in -y change to -ier in the comparative: 'easy' becomes 'easier.'

quests.partialSentence: Our new office is ____ than the old building downtown.
quests.hint: This adjective has more than one syllable, so think about how the comparative is formed.
quests.explanation: Longer adjectives like 'modern' usually take 'more' instead of an -er ending.

quests.partialSentence: My new manager is ____ than the previous one.
quests.hint: This adjective ends in -y, so look at how that changes in the comparative.
quests.explanation: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y typically change to -ier: 'friendly' becomes 'friendlier.'

quests.partialSentence: We still have ____ time before our flight, so let's relax.
quests.hint: This is a positive sentence, so think about the quantifier we use for an unspecified amount.
quests.explanation: 'Some' is used in positive sentences for an unspecified, usually moderate, amount.

quests.partialSentence: There isn't ____ luggage space left in the car trunk.
quests.hint: This is a negative sentence, so think about the quantifier that pairs with 'isn't.'
quests.explanation: 'Any' is used in negative sentences, fitting after 'isn't' to mean none at all.

quests.partialSentence: We met ____ interesting travelers at the hostel last night.
quests.hint: This is a positive sentence describing an unspecified number of people.
quests.explanation: 'Some' fits positive sentences describing an unspecified quantity, here a number of travelers.

quests.partialSentence: Do you have ____ photos from your cousin's wedding?
quests.hint: This is a question, so think about the quantifier commonly used there.
quests.explanation: 'Any' is the natural choice in questions asking whether something exists.

quests.partialSentence: My uncle has ____ stories about his childhood in the countryside.
quests.hint: This is a positive statement about an unspecified number of stories.
quests.explanation: 'Some' fits positive statements describing an unspecified, fairly large number.

quests.partialSentence: There is ____ reason to worry; everyone in the family is doing fine.
quests.hint: Think about a quantifier that means zero, used to reassure someone.
quests.explanation: 'No' means zero amount and is often used to reassure someone that nothing is wrong.

quests.partialSentence: The big winter sale always starts ____ December.
quests.hint: Think about the preposition we use with months.
quests.explanation: 'In' is used with months, such as 'in December' or 'in July.'

quests.partialSentence: The shop closes early ____ Sundays.
quests.hint: Think about the preposition we use with days of the week.
quests.explanation: 'On' is used with specific days, such as 'on Sundays.'

quests.partialSentence: Most online orders arrive ____ five business days.
quests.hint: Think about a preposition meaning 'before this period of time ends.'
quests.explanation: 'Within' is used to express a time limit, meaning before a period ends, such as 'within five days.'

quests.partialSentence: We always eat a big family dinner ____ New Year's Eve.
quests.hint: Think about the preposition used with specific calendar dates or named days.
quests.explanation: 'On' is used with specific days or dates, such as 'on New Year's Eve.'

quests.partialSentence: The restaurant serves a special menu ____ the holiday season.
quests.hint: Think about the preposition meaning 'throughout a period of time.'
quests.explanation: 'During' is used to describe something happening throughout a period, such as a season.

quests.partialSentence: Breakfast is served ____ seven o'clock every morning.
quests.hint: Think about the preposition we use with exact clock times.
quests.explanation: 'At' is used with precise times, such as 'at seven o'clock.'
